column5: “Token passthrough” is an anti-pattern where an MCP server accepts tokens from an MCP client without validating that the tokens were properly issued to the MCP server and passes them through to the downstream API.

column3: Accepting tokens issued for other services breaks a fundamental OAuth security boundary and lets attackers reuse legitimate tokens across different services than intended (`mcp-security-best-practices#token-passthrough`).
